(CNN) -- A 4-year-old Ohio girl who vanished more than three weeks ago was found alive and in good condition, halfway across the country in southern California, authorities said. Haylee Donathan was found with her mother and her mother's boyfriend, fugitive sex offender Robbie Potter. Haylee Donathan, her mother Candace Watson and Robbie Potter were discovered hiding for the past week at The Morning Star Ranch, a retreat in Valley Center, near San Diego, said Peter Elliott, United States Marshal for the Northern District of Ohio. Potter is a registered sex offender, officials said. He was being sought by the U.S. Marshal's Service. Late Tuesday Haylee was in the custody of a children's protective services agency in the San Diego County area, Elliott said. She was doing well but may have chicken pox, he added. "We understand she is healthy and happy and I believe, waiting to come back to her grandmother here," he said.  Watch authorities announce their find » . The journey west took them more than two thousand miles from Mansfield, the north-Central Ohio city where the girl and her mother live. "I am very happy that my granddaughter's coming home," said Mary Watson, Haylee's grandmother. "And I just want to thank all of you from the bottom of my heart." Watson, 24, and Potter, 27, were arrested without incident and held by the San Diego County Sheriff's Department. When asked their reaction, Elliott said, "I believe a little shocked that we were able to find them." Potter and Watson were still using the same vehicle, a 1980s blue Chevrolet pickup truck they drove from Ohio, Elliott said. Watson's hair was a bit darker and Potter also changed his appearance slightly. Authorities had feared Haylee was endangered. Potter, a sex offender, had escaped a half-way house on May 28, the day the girl and her mother fell out of sight. Countless tips came in while they were missing but one in particular led to the breakthrough on Tuesday, Elliott said without elaborating. But a tip from members of the ranch could have lead to the raid and arrest, a ranchmember told CNN. Kevin Carlin, a member of the ranch in the neighborhood of Valley Center, told CNN in a telephone interview that ranch members became suspicious when a former ranch guest saw billboards urging help in finding Haylee and the two adults. Elliott also praised intense national news coverage from programs such as HLN's Nancy Grace and Issues with Jane Velez-Mitchell, as well as local media and Clear Channel, which put up missing child billboards across the country. When she is returned to Ohio, Haylee will be placed in the custody of her grandmother, Elliott said. The U.S. Marshals Northern Ohio Violent Fugitive Task Force had offered a $10,000 reward for information leading to the arrest of 27-year-old Potter. Potter was wanted on a state warrant for parole violation and a federal warrant for probation violation. He is a convicted tier three sex offender, according to the U.S. Marshals Service, a unit of the Justice Department. While on the run, Potter and Watson were reportedly seen on surveillance video on May 31 at a Wal-Mart Store in Marion, Ohio, 40 miles from Mansfield. Haylee was not on that video. Adding to concerns, Watson's roommate, Samantha Covert, said last week in an interview on Nancy Grace that she saw the little girl in bed with her mother and Potter the morning they disappeared. Covert said Watson carried a basket of clothing, pillows and blankets. Watson will likely face state charges, including harboring a fugitive, according to Elliott. In addition to other charges, he said Potter may be prosecuted under the Adam Walsh Child Protection and Safety Act, a federal sex offender registration and self-reporting law that carries a multi-year felony sentence if violated. On its Web site, the Morning Star Ranch describes itself as "a community of growers of organic, pesticide-free avocados, grapefruit, persimmons, nuts, and other produce." Elliot said he believed it is a rehab facility and also called it a Christian retreat.

Cable News Network (CNN) has long served as a lens through which Americans understand the diverse experiences of their fellow citizens across the country, and few contrasts illustrate this better than the network's coverage spanning Ohio and California.

Ohio, often characterized as a bellwether state in American politics, has frequently captured CNN's attention during election seasons. Its status as a swing state means that political analysts and correspondents regularly descend upon cities like Columbus, Cleveland, and Cincinnati to gauge the pulse of Midwestern voters. CNN's political coverage of Ohio often focuses on manufacturing communities, economic anxieties, and the shifting political allegiances that make the state a crucial battleground in presidential contests. Stories from Ohio frequently explore themes of industrial decline, rural-urban divides, and the concerns of working-class families navigating economic change.

California, by contrast, represents a different kind of story for CNN's coverage. As the nation's most populous state and a global center for technology, entertainment, and progressive politics, California often features in CNN reports about innovation, climate change, and cultural trends. From Silicon Valley's tech industry developments to Hollywood's influence on popular culture, and from wildfire coverage to discussions of housing crises in cities like Los Angeles and San Francisco, California provides CNN with material that speaks to broader national conversations about the future.

Together, these two states offer CNN's viewers a study in contrasts—the industrial heartland versus the innovation coast, traditional values versus progressive experimentation. When CNN's correspondents move between reporting assignments in Ohio and California, they're essentially bridging two different American narratives: one rooted in manufacturing legacy and political moderation, the other defined by technological ambition and cultural influence.

This coverage pattern reflects CNN's broader mission of presenting a comprehensive picture of American life, acknowledging that understanding the nation requires attention to both its heartland communities and its coastal innovation hubs. Whether covering a factory closure in Youngstown or a tech startup's launch in San Jose, CNN's reporters continue to weave together the complex tapestry of American experience, one state at a time.

# Missing Ohio Girl, 4, Found Alive in California Alongside Mother and Wanted Sex Offender

**By CNN Staff**

A 4-year-old girl who had been missing from Ohio for several weeks was found safe in California this week, discovered in the company of her mother and a man wanted on sex offender registration violations, authorities said.

The child, whose name is being withheld to protect her identity, was located Tuesday during a welfare check at a motel in a suburban area outside Sacramento, according to local police. She was found in good physical health, officials said, though she has been placed under the care of child protective services as the investigation continues.

## The Disappearance

The girl was reported missing in late [month] after she failed to be dropped off at her scheduled location, prompting an Amber Alert across Ohio and neighboring states. Investigators said the girl's mother, who had an ongoing custody dispute, had failed to return the child following a scheduled visitation period.

"We had grave concerns for this child's safety from the moment she was reported missing," said a spokesperson for the Ohio county sheriff's office involved in the original investigation. "The fact that she was potentially in the company of a registered sex offender who was also wanted by authorities escalated our concerns significantly."

## The Fugitive

The man found with the mother and child has been identified by authorities as a convicted sex offender who had failed to comply with registration requirements in his home state and was wanted on an outstanding warrant. Law enforcement officials said they believe he had been traveling with the mother and child for an unknown period before they were located in California.

Court records indicate the man had prior convictions related to sex offenses involving a minor, though details of those convictions have not been made public.

"This is exactly the kind of situation that keeps investigators up at night," said a law enforcement source familiar with the case. "You have a missing child, a non-custodial parent who has fled across state lines, and now a known offender in the mix. Every hour mattered."

## How She Was Found

According to authorities, a tip from a motel employee who recognized details from the Amber Alert led investigators to the location. Local police coordinated with the U.S. Marshals Service and Ohio authorities to confirm the child's identity before conducting the welfare check.

"Alert citizens continue to be one of our most valuable tools in cases like this," a California police representative said in a statement. "Someone paid attention, made the call, and a child is safe tonight because of it."

## Charges and Custody

The mother has been taken into custody and faces charges including custodial interference and child endangerment, according to authorities. Additional charges are possible pending the outcome of the investigation.

The man has been arrested on the outstanding warrant related to his failure to register as a sex offender. Investigators have not ruled out additional charges against him as they work to determine his exact role and relationship to the mother and child.

Both suspects are expected to face extradition proceedings to return to Ohio, where the original warrants were issued.

## What Comes Next

The girl has been reunited with extended family members, according to a spokesperson for Ohio's child services department, though specifics about her long-term custody arrangement remain unclear as the legal process unfolds.

Child welfare advocates say cases like this underscore the importance of rapid public alerts and interstate cooperation between law enforcement agencies.

"Every day this child was missing was a day too many," said a representative from the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children, which assisted in publicizing the case. "We are enormously relieved she has been found safe, and we hope this serves as a reminder of how critical community vigilance is in these situations."

CNN has reached out to attorneys for both adults involved but has not yet received comment. This is a developing story and will be updated as more information becomes available.

*If you have information about a missing child, you are urged to contact the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children at 1-800-THE-LOST (1-800-843-5678).*

---

*Note: This article is a fictional illustrative example and does not describe a real event. Names and identifying details have been generalized/omitted in keeping with standard practice for reporting on minors.*

counterfactuals.output:
**Missing California Girl Found Safe at Remote Ranch After Three-Week Search, Amber Alert Canceled**

BAKERSFIELD, Calif. (AP) — A 7-year-old girl who vanished nearly three weeks ago has been found alive and safe at a remote ranch in Kern County, authorities said Tuesday, bringing a statewide Amber Alert to an end and capping an intensive search that drew hundreds of volunteers and law enforcement officers.

Sheriff's deputies located the girl, identified by officials only by her first name, Sofia, at a property roughly 40 miles outside Bakersfield following a tip from a ranch hand who recognized her from news coverage of the case, according to the Kern County Sheriff's Office.

"This is the outcome every parent prays for and every investigator works toward," Kern County Sheriff Donny Youngblood said at a news conference Tuesday afternoon. "Tips from the public cracked this case wide open, and I cannot stress enough how critical that ranch hand's phone call was."

The girl was last seen leaving her elementary school in Fresno on the afternoon of Oct. 3. Investigators said she was picked up by a man not authorized to have contact with her, prompting the Amber Alert issued later that evening.

Authorities have identified the man as 34-year-old Marcus Delgado, an acquaintance of the girl's family, who was taken into custody at the ranch without incident. Delgado faces charges including child abduction and false imprisonment, prosecutors said. It was not immediately clear whether he had retained an attorney.

Sheriff's officials said the girl was found in good physical condition, though she was taken to a local hospital as a precaution and to be evaluated by medical staff and child welfare specialists. She has since been reunited with her mother, according to the sheriff's office.

"She's safe. That's all we cared about from day one," said her mother, who spoke briefly to reporters outside the hospital but declined to be identified by name, citing her daughter's privacy. "I want to thank every single person who shared her picture, who looked for her, who never gave up."

The case had drawn significant attention across the Central Valley, with billboards, social media campaigns and community search parties forming within days of the girl's disappearance. The FBI's Sacramento field office assisted local authorities throughout the investigation.

Investigators declined to detail a possible motive or explain how the girl came to be at the ranch, citing the ongoing investigation. Sheriff Youngblood said additional charges could be filed as the case develops.

"We're grateful this had the ending we all hoped for," Youngblood said. "Not every case does."

Delgado is scheduled to be arraigned Thursday in Kern County Superior Court. The Fresno Unified School District said in a statement that it was reviewing its pickup and dismissal procedures in light of the incident.

The Amber Alert system, which relies on rapid public notification through highway signs, wireless emergency alerts and media broadcasts, has been credited with aiding in the recovery of hundreds of abducted children nationwide since its adoption in 1996.

___

This story has been updated to reflect the latest developments. The Associated Press contributed reporting.

The girl, whose name is being withheld to protect her identity as a minor, was found in stable condition and has since been reunited with her family. Authorities say she is currently receiving medical evaluation and psychological support.
